root.name: Nimzo-Indian Defense: Ragozin Variation
root.moves: 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 e6 3. Nc3 Bb4 4. e3 O-O 5. Bd3 d5 6. Nf3 Nc6 7. O-O dxc4

overview: This is the Nimzo-Indian reached by 4.e3 O-O 5.Bd3 d5 6.Nf3 Nc6 7.O-O dxc4, Black taking the pawn, with 8.Bxc4 Bd6 as the normal follow-up. White has the centre and bishop pair chances, Black has solid development and pressure on e4 and d4 with ...e5 breaks. The structure is classical and positional, with an IQP only if the centre is traded.

white_ideas.idea: Recapture with Bxc4 and play e4 or Qe2 with a strong centre
Aim for central breaks and a kingside initiative

typical_structures.structure: Classical d4/e3 centre with Black pressure on the d-pawn

character.notes: Positional play in a balanced Nimzo line; neither side is forced into sharp play.

gambit.notes: Black's ...dxc4 pawn comes back with Bxc4, so it is not a gambit.

structure.notes: Tension in the centre that can resolve to open or IQP structures.

approach.notes: A main line of the Nimzo, standard.

level.notes: Understanding of central breaks and piece placement, with modest theory.
